originalConceptPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: polished game-map redesign concept, wide landscape image.
Input image 1 is the edit target and layout/content reference: a factory-themed educational game map with five named stations and numbered levels.
Primary request: completely art-direct this map into one cohesive, beautifully composed illustrated factory campus. Main stations must clearly stand out, and supporting digital art must physically lead the eye from station to station rather than look like scattered unrelated stickers.

Preserve the five building identities, names, distinctive accent colors, and general layout: blue Receiving upper left, purple Packing upper middle, orange Warehouse upper right, green Shipping lower right, cyan Lab lower left. Preserve the friendly dimensional isometric mobile-game art style and level-map purpose, but substantially improve visual hierarchy and composition. The attached screenshot is reference, not a frame to place inside the new image.

Composition: full-bleed wide landscape, approximately 1.94:1. Show the complete map with generous safe margins. Five large, detailed hero buildings, each grounded on a matching cream stone / blue-gray paved campus platform, with integrated landscaping and neatly grouped relevant equipment. Each building should be much larger than any prop. Clear, readable nameplates centered with their buildings. Keep the center airy. Build a single continuous flowing campus and progression route across the top left-to-right, curving around the right edge, then traveling back toward the lower left. Make station-to-station connections readable and elegant, keeping substantial breathing room around buildings and level controls.

Supporting artwork: replace every disconnected oversized item with small purposeful connected scenes. A low conveyor carrying a few crates connects Receiving to Packing; a packing line and organized pallet transfer connect Packing to Warehouse; a compact loading lane with storage bays guides down to Shipping; a tidy service conduit / inspection conveyor guides from Shipping toward Lab. These connections sit alongside the navigation path, physically meet the station platforms, share one consistent isometric perspective, and smoothly continue between districts. Add only a few small crates, gantries, pipes and loading tools where their function makes visual sense, all at consistent scale. No giant floating boxes, giant isolated pipe elbows or random freestanding art. Supporting art is less saturated and smaller than the five stations.

Navigation UI: retain a clear navy-blue serpentine route with glossy blue circular numbered level markers and restrained gold star badges. Include the level sequence 1 through 30 once each, in travel order. Group 1-4 with Receiving; 5-9 with Packing; 10-15 with Warehouse; 16-21 with Shipping; 22-30 with Lab. Lower row runs right to left, so progression continues naturally from the right-hand bend toward Lab. Levels 1-21 completed in blue with small gold star accents; level 22 active with a gold ring and tiny 'You are here' label; levels 23-30 muted pale blue with tiny locks. Number markers remain legible and distinct from illustration, with no overlaps over buildings. Route is subordinate to hero buildings but navigation remains obvious.

Text verbatim: 'Receiving', 'Packing', 'Warehouse', 'Shipping', 'Lab', 'You are here', numerals 1 through 30. Use crisp friendly sans-serif lettering, white station text on compact deep blue nameplates. No extra titles, headings, logos or watermarks.

Art direction: high quality stylized 3D isometric illustration, one coherent camera angle, soft light from upper left, consistent ambient shadows, crisp well-crafted silhouettes, attractive beveled details, calm mint/sage ground, subtle grass islands and small clustered trees only around edges. Soft quiet background with no ghost buildings or fog overlay. Rich coordinated blue/navy foundations, warm golden crate details, controlled individual station accents. Beautiful, finished game UI concept rather than a rough diagram. The outcome should feel like five memorable destinations within one connected working factory world.
